grand_strategy.reading: Eritrea runs the strategy of a garrison state that has turned isolation into method: an army with no end date, a constitution never applied, and a ring of partners (Egypt, Somalia, Sudan, with Russia at the UN) built to keep Ethiopia off the Red Sea. The structural problem is that it holds the coast and the port that Ethiopia wants, so each Ethiopian move on Assab reads in Asmara as an attack, and each Eritrean move in Tigray reads in Addis as an invasion. The 1-2 October 2026 rupture shows the paradox at full size: the ring is Addis Ababa's proof of encirclement, and the 'no war, no peace' that Asmara kept from 2000 to 2018 is ending on the border.

stances.note: Adversary (review regrade from rival, 2026-10-16): since 1 Oct 2026 each state reads the other as a mortal threat. Ethiopia shut its embassy in Asmara and expelled Eritrean diplomats for 'acts of hostility and belligerence', Eritrea severed relations in reply, Addis Ababa told the Security Council on 8-9 Oct that Eritrean troops had advanced up to 60 km into Tigray and invoked Article 51, and says Asmara arms the coalition whose declared aim is the overthrow of its government; Asmara answers that Ethiopia has 'declared war' to seize Assab, which would end Eritrea as a coastal state. Mutual aims of regime change on one side and territorial amputation on the other are the atlas's test for adversary, so the grade mirrors Ethiopia's reading. Against: Abiy said in March 2026 that Ethiopia would not go to war over sea access, and the 2000-2018 'no war, no peace' was graded rivalry; confidence C, all sources tier 3. Bond grievance (the 1998-2000 war, the Assab claim), not kin.

stances.note: Border legacy: armed clashes at Ras Doumeira (Gabla) and the Doumeira island in June 2008; UN measures on Eritrea from December 2009 (resolution 1907); Qatari mediation from 2010, which ended with Eritrea's pull-back and no demarcation. The 2018 Ethiopian-led thaw did not settle the border. The current alignment runs the other way: Djibouti leans toward Eritrea and Egypt on the Red Sea (Africa Confidential, January 2026), but it earns about USD 1.5bn a year from Ethiopia's use of its port, which is why it is not a partner. Rival, confidence C: the grade is our reading of an unresolved border; no Eritrean or Djiboutian source uses the word. The 2008 casualty figures are contested and not used here.

stances.note: Lavrov's surprise visit to Asmara (27 January 2023) sought Eritrean support on Ukraine; Isaias made an official visit to Moscow in May-June 2023 and attended the Russia-Africa summit in St Petersburg in July 2023. Partner, not ally: no treaty. The UN record (dataset, not written here) has Eritrea voting with Russia on five of six Ukraine landmark votes, including 2 March 2022, when Eritrea, Russia, Belarus, DPRK and Syria voted no; on ES-11/4 (October 2022) Eritrea abstained while Russia voted no. Its voting affinity with Russia (0.69, 2022-26) is below the all-member average (about 0.78). Bond affinity: shared hostility to a 'unipolar' order (Isaias, Moscow 2023), not kinship. Trend warming on the 2023 visits.

stances.note: Red Sea rivalry, not a will to destroy. The UAE's Assab base (2015-2021) ended when it left the Yemen front; no 2026 presence or agreement was found. In 2026 the UAE sits on the Ethiopian and Somaliland side of the Red Sea divide (Africa Confidential, January 2026), against Eritrea, Egypt and Somalia, and Somalia cancelled its UAE agreements in January 2026. Rival, cooling, confidence C: our reading of the structure; no Eritrean source uses the word. The ARE card reads Eritrea as partner (cooling, confidence C). The two readings disagree and are the item to resolve in review: the base is gone, but the Red Sea alignment now puts the UAE on Ethiopia's side. Bond none.
